From 373e715e31bf4e0f129befe87613a278fac228d3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Kirill A. Shutemov" <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Oct 2022 17:12:20 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] x86/tdx: Panic on bad configs that #VE on "private" memory
 access

All normal kernel memory is "TDX private memory".  This includes
everything from kernel stacks to kernel text.  Handling
exceptions on arbitrary accesses to kernel memory is essentially
impossible because they can happen in horribly nasty places like
kernel entry/exit.  But, TDX hardware can theoretically _deliver_
a virtualization exception (#VE) on any access to private memory.

But, it's not as bad as it sounds.  TDX can be configured to never
deliver these exceptions on private memory with a "TD attribute"
called ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE.  The guest has no way to *set* this
attribute, but it can check it.

Ensure ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE is set in early boot.  panic() if it
is unset.  There is no sane way for Linux to run with this
attribute clear so a panic() is appropriate.

There's small window during boot before the check where kernel
has an early #VE handler. But the handler is only for port I/O
and will also panic() as soon as it sees any other #VE, such as
a one generated by a private memory access.

diff --git a/arch/x86/coco/tdx/tdx.c b/arch/x86/coco/tdx/tdx.c
index 3fee96931ff5..b8998cf0508a 100644
--- a/arch/x86/coco/tdx/tdx.c
+++ b/arch/x86/coco/tdx/tdx.c
@@ -34,6 +34,8 @@
 #define VE_GET_PORT_NUM(e)	((e) >> 16)
 #define VE_IS_IO_STRING(e)	((e) & BIT(4))
 
+#define ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE	BIT(28)
+
 /*
  * Wrapper for standard use of __tdx_hypercall with no output aside from
  * return code.
@@ -102,6 +104,7 @@ static void tdx_parse_tdinfo(u64 *cc_mask)
 {
 	struct tdx_module_output out;
 	unsigned int gpa_width;
+	u64 td_attr;
 
 	/*
 	 * TDINFO TDX module call is used to get the TD execution environment
@@ -109,19 +112,27 @@ static void tdx_parse_tdinfo(u64 *cc_mask)
 	 * information, etc. More details about the ABI can be found in TDX
 	 * Guest-Host-Communication Interface (GHCI), section 2.4.2 TDCALL
 	 * [TDG.VP.INFO].
-	 *
-	 * The GPA width that comes out of this call is critical. TDX guests
-	 * can not meaningfully run without it.
 	 */
 	tdx_module_call(TDX_GET_INFO, 0, 0, 0, 0, &out);
 
-	gpa_width = out.rcx & GENMASK(5, 0);
-
 	/*
 	 * The highest bit of a guest physical address is the "sharing" bit.
 	 * Set it for shared pages and clear it for private pages.
+	 *
+	 * The GPA width that comes out of this call is critical. TDX guests
+	 * can not meaningfully run without it.
 	 */
+	gpa_width = out.rcx & GENMASK(5, 0);
 	*cc_mask = BIT_ULL(gpa_width - 1);
+
+	/*
+	 * The kernel can not handle #VE's when accessing normal kernel
+	 * memory.  Ensure that no #VE will be delivered for accesses to
+	 * TD-private memory.  Only VMM-shared memory (MMIO) will #VE.
+	 */
+	td_attr = out.rdx;
+	if (!(td_attr & ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE))
+		panic("TD misconfiguration: SEPT_VE_DISABLE attibute must be set.\n");
 }
 
 /*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/coco/tdx/tdx.c`**
   - Added a new macro definition: `#define ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE	BIT(28)`.
   - Introduced a new variable `u64 td_attr;` to store the TD attributes.
   - Modified the `tdx_parse_tdinfo` function to include a check for the `ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE` attribute:
     - After retrieving the TD information, it checks if `td_attr` has the `ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE` bit set.
     - If the bit is not set, the function calls `panic()` with an error message indicating a misconfiguration.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `tdx.c` are aimed at ensuring that the TDX (Trusted Domain Extensions) environment is correctly configured to prevent virtualization exceptions (#VE) on accesses to private memory. The addition of the `ATTR_SEPT_VE_DISABLE` check is crucial because it enforces a requirement that the kernel must not handle #VE exceptions for normal kernel memory accesses. If this attribute is not set during early boot, the system will panic, indicating that it cannot safely operate under such conditions. This change is a safeguard against potential misconfigurations that could lead to instability or security issues in the TDX environment.
